blocks.en: Note that by using the calculations of \eqref{eq:dirichlet-variational-integration-by-parts} (though this time with a function $v\in H_0^k(\Omega)$ in place of $\phi\in\mathcal{D}(\Omega)$) we can see that any strong solution of the Dirichlet problem is automatically a weak solution. However, since we require so much less smoothness of weak solutions than strong ones, it will be far easier to show that weak solutions exist. Once we have done this, we will be able to show that if $\Omega$, $f$ and the coefficients $a_{\sigma\gamma}$ are sufficiently ``nice,\textquotesingle\textquotesingle\ the weak solution is, in fact, a strong solution or a classical solution.
blocks.zh: 注意, 利用 \eqref{eq:dirichlet-variational-integration-by-parts} 中的计算 (不过这次以函数 $v\in H_0^k(\Omega)$ 取代 $\phi\in\mathcal{D}(\Omega)$), 可见 Dirichlet 问题的任意强解自然也是弱解. 然而, 由于对弱解的光滑性要求远低于强解, 证明弱解存在会容易得多. 做到这一点后, 将能证明: 若 $\Omega$, $f$ 和系数 $a_{\sigma\gamma}$ 足够 ``好\textquotesingle\textquotesingle, 则弱解事实上是强解或经典解.
